messages:
sasha: Heads-up — customer reported that the deployment-manager role can no longer rotate KMS keys after yesterday's RBAC refactor. Seen this elsewhere? :eyes:

ana: Ack. Any error logs or request IDs we can follow up with?

sasha: Error from the API when calling /v1/kms/keys/{key_id}: 403 Forbidden. Customer says the token has the deployment-manager role bound. They can still create deployments but not rotate keys.

kevin: Is this the new role -> permission mapping change? I remember we collapsed a few perms into `kms.manage` last week. Maybe the role didn't get the new permission.

liz: I just reproduced locally with a service account: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/kms/keys/key123/rotate
Response: {"error":"forbidden","message":"missing permission: kms.rotate"}

kevin: That explains it. deployment-manager previously had kms.rotate explicitly. During refactor we replaced kms.rotate + kms.read -> kms.manage but forgot to map deployment-manager to kms.manage.

ana: Can we patch the db role mappings quickly? Which files define the bootstrap bindings? I can push a hotfix to the config store.

kevin: Bindings live in infra/auth/role_bindings.yaml and the runtime checks map perms -> capability in authz/service_roles.go. Need both updated. Quick mitigation: add a temporary policy binding for the team:  

```
# temporary emergency binding
bindings:
  - role: deployment-manager
    permissions:
      - kms.manage
```

sasha: If we add kms.manage right away, will that create any unexpected escalation (e.g., allow key deletions)? What does kms.manage include?

kevin: kms.manage currently = [kms.read, kms.rotate, kms.encrypt, kms.decrypt]. Key deletion is a separate permission kms.admin which we didn't include. So should be safe for now.

liz: I'm going to add the binding to the staging config and run the signing job to verify. Will report back in 10m. :clock10:

audit-bot: Note: audit pipeline did not emit any kms.rotate events for the failed request id=rc_41f2. Investigating ingestion.

ana: Re: audit — that's concerning. Even failed authz checks should be logged. Is the authz check happening before audit hook?

kevin: Good point. I dug into authz middleware — there's a short-circuit when an RBAC cache miss occurs, and we return 403 without emitting to the audit queue. That was an optimization added to reduce noise. We should still log misses as "authz_denied" events.

sasha: This is both a correctness and observability gap. Customers expect to see failed key rotations in audit logs. We need a two-step plan: 1) emergency permission patch, 2) audit fix + add regression test.

liz: Staging patch applied, rotate call now returns 202 Accepted for the service account. I pushed a small change to role_bindings.yaml (staging) and rolled the config; smoke tests OK.

kevin: I'll open a PR to update the canonical infra file and the service_roles.go mapping so deployment-manager maps to kms.manage. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1298

ana: I'll add an e2e test to devops/tests/rbac that asserts: when role=deployment-manager, kms.rotate is allowed and appears in audit events. Test skeleton: 

```
it "deployment-manager can rotate key and audit logs the attempt" do
  token = create_token_with_role("deployment-manager")
  rotate_resp = api.rotate_key(token, key_id)
  expect(rotate_resp.status).to eq(202)
  logs = audit.fetch_events(request_id: rotate_resp.request_id)
  expect(logs.map(&:type)).to include("authz_allowed", "kms.rotate")
end
```

sasha: Nice. Can you also update the SDK doc page that lists roles/permissions? A lot of customers reference that. Location: docs/security/rbac.md. Add a changelog entry noting the refactor and mapping changes.

kevin: Will do. Also adding a migration note for teams that had custom roles referencing kms.rotate to move to kms.manage if they want the grouped permission.

audit-bot: Audit pipeline fix: ingestion now emits authz_denied for cache-miss paths. Patch deployed to logging-worker at 1795409500. Monitoring for 30m.

liz: FYI, I saw one downstream failure in a CI job where a test expected missing audit events; we need to update tests that asserted absence. I'll send a separate PR to fix CI.

ana: Filing an internal incident ticket for tracking: INC-2026 (RBAC/KMS rotation + audit misses). I'll add owners: @kevin, @liz.

sasha: Thanks team. After infra PR merges, let's cut a short internal note and email to customers who reported this. Also mark as P1 until audit logs confirmed.

kevin: PR opened, tagging eng-runtime and eng-security. Will link to the ticket when CI passes.

sasha: Closing loop: please add a one-line summary to the incident ticket once you ship the infra change + docs update. :lock:
